findings.claim: BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.isValid() (the fixture provider) accepts any stored recovery code in any order and never consumes it. Federated recovery codes are therefore reusable, the sequential 'code #N' behaviour is not enforced, and the exhausted-credential cleanup path is never reached.

verifier.reason: In testsuite/.../federation/BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.java:326-340 the recovery-codes branch of isValid() returns `generatedKeys.stream().anyMatch(key -> key.equals(input.getChallengeResponse()))` and never mutates `myUser.recoveryCodes`, so any stored code validates in any order and repeatedly. getCredentials() (lines 231-246) rebuilds the model from the full list each call, so `allCodesUsed()` at RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator.java:85 is never true for this provider.

findings.claim: Core Keycloak does not enforce single use for recovery codes stored through the generic user-storage path. It leaves consuming a used code entirely to the user-storage provider, with no guidance.

verifier.reason: For a federated user, model/storage/src/main/java/org/keycloak/credential/UserCredentialManager.java:66-77 lets the storage provider's validator accept the code and drop it from the list, so the only code-consuming logic (services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/credential/RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProvider.java:110-111) never runs. services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authentication/authenticators/browser/RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator.java:80-92 afterwards only checks allCodesUsed() and never marks the used code, and the patch adds no docs or javadoc telling providers to do so (its own sample provider just does anyMatch over all codes without removal).

findings.claim: The changed User Storage SPI contract for recovery codes is not documented anywhere. getCredentials must return Keycloak's internal hashed RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel format, while updateCredential receives plaintext codes.

verifier.reason: The patch sends plaintext codes as JSON to the storage's `updateCredential` (server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/utils/CredentialHelper.java:119-125), while the readers parse the federated credential's credentialData/secretData as the hashed `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel` format (server-spi/src/main/java/org/keycloak/models/utils/RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.java:56-61, RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator.java:80-84). The patch adds no docs, and neither the `getCredentials` javadoc (server-spi/src/main/java/org/keycloak/credential/CredentialInputUpdater.java:43-52) nor anything under docs/ (recovery-codes.adoc, 26_2_0.adoc:84-98) describes this contract.

findings.claim: updateCredential receives the recovery codes as a plaintext JSON list in challengeResponse, whereas the local store keeps them hashed.

verifier.reason: server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/utils/CredentialHelper.java:119-125 serialises the raw generatedCodes to JSON and passes them as the challengeResponse of a UserCredentialModel to updateCredential, whereas the local-store model is built by RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromValues, which hashes each code via hashRawCode (server-spi/src/main/java/org/keycloak/models/credential/RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.java:65-67). This mirrors how raw passwords are handed to user storage, so hashing is left to the federated provider.

findings.claim: RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator takes the credential returned by getCredential(), which may come from user storage, makes the allCodesUsed decision on it, and calls removeStoredCredentialById(). That method only removes local/fed-storage credentials, so the provider's copy is not removed. When local and federated credentials both exist, the authenticator inspects or removes a different credential from the one that validated.

verifier.reason: RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator.java:80-87 now takes the credential from RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential() (federated-first, RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.java:57-63), checks allCodesUsed on it and calls removeStoredCredentialById, which only reaches the local/federated-storage UserCredentialStore (UserCredentialManager.java:114-117, 298-305), never the user storage provider. Validation can instead succeed against the locally stored credential (UserCredentialManager.java:66-77; RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProvider.java:101), so when both exist the inspected/removed credential can differ from the one that validated.

findings.claim: Recovery-code credentials from federated user storage are now read before local ones, which changes the order of precedence.

verifier.reason: `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential` (server-spi/src/main/java/org/keycloak/models/utils/RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.java:56-61) reads `getFederatedCredentialsStream()` first and only falls back to local `getStoredCredentialsByTypeStream`, and it replaces the previous local-only lookups in RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator.java:80 and RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean.java:17. findings.claim: In the fixture's getCredentials(), the recovery-codes model is rebuilt with RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromValues(), which does not set an id. The returned credential has a null id and the codes are renumbered, so removal by id (removeStoredCredentialById, admin/account deletion) fails.
